newsitem.title: UK: Clyde rejects raised Gulf Canada bid.
newsitem.headline: Clyde rejects raised Gulf Canada bid.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd Tuesday raised its hostile bid for Clyde Petroleum Plc, but the British oil exploration and production firm spurned the increased offer as inadequate.
Gulf Canada increased its bid to 120 pence per share from 105 pence per share, saying the new 494.6 million pound ($793 million) offer was final.
However Gulf's new offer, which topped previous offer of 432 million pounds ($693 million), was below the 125 pence a share level some analysts had been looking for.
Gulf said it reserved the right to raise its offer further if a rival bidder emerged -- which some analysts believe could now happen.

"This is a substantial increase for Clyde shareholders," Gulf chief executive J.P. Bryan said in a statement. "It provides cash now for a company with little or no upside due to its lack of exploration success and potential -- a company which, based on its own forecast, will in 1997 show almost no growth in discretionary cash flow."
Bryan said later that there was a danger Gulf Canada could pay too high a price for Clyde.
"Gulf could be paying too much if commodity prices go into a downdraught. That is a risk we are prepared to take," he told reporters in a conference call.
In the increasingly bitter war of words between the two companies, Bryan accused Clyde of having low reserves, failing to replace production and being over-dependent on acquisitions.
But Clyde hit back, urging shareholders to reject the bid, which it said significantly undervalued the company.

"Clyde is worth a great deal more than this offer. We recommend that shareholders do not accept this predatory attempt at depriving them of full value for their Clyde shares," Clyde Chairman Malcolm Gourlay said in a statement.
Clyde said the new offer represented only 4.3 times its forecast 1997 cash flow, adding that this was a lower multiple than any of its British peers.
Clyde has previously accused Gulf Canada of undervaluing it in terms of its cash flow multiple, a favoured method for valuing oil companies in North America.
The company also said the net asset value of its existing assets was 120 pence to 144 pence before a premium for a going concern, according to an independent evaluation.
Clyde Petroleum's shares gained 2.5 pence to 120p and ranked among the most heavily traded stocks on the London Stock Exchange during early business.
